    CITY OF INGLEWOOD
  Parking and Traffic Commission
  One West Manchester Blvd., Inglewood, CA 90301
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  Wednesday, February 22, 2023 at 7:00 pm
  JANUARY 2023 MEETING MINUTES

1. Roll Call
A. A meeting was held on the 1st floor in Conference Room A at 7:03 pm in City Hall. Commissioner Charles
  Braggs, District 1, serves as interim chairperson until further notice.
B. Attendees included:
 Charles Braggs, Commissioner, District 1 & Acting as Chairperson
 Kip Rudd, Commissioner, District 2
 Brett C.S. Roberts, Commissioner, District 3
 Lois Hale, Commissioner, District 4
 William Thompson, LAZ Parking Traffic Operations Manager
 Lieutenant David Salcedo, City of Inglewood Police Department
 Peter Puglese, City of Inglewood Traffic Engineer
 Raquel Méndez, Secretary
C. Opening
  Commissioner Charles Braggs opened the first meeting of 2023 by greeting the audience and introducing
  the new District 4 Commissioner, Lois Hale. Additionally, Commissioner Charles Braggs announced the
  passing of Michael Benbow, Chairperson. Mr. Michael Benbow served on the City of Inglewood Traffic
  and Parking Commission committee for over fourteen years. In addition, he played a significant role as a
  mentor to the committee members and the community.

2. Approval of Minutes
A. October 2022 Meeting Minutes
 Commissioner Kid Rudd made a motion to accept the meeting notes. Seconded by Commissioner Brett
  C.S. Roberts. Commissioner Lois Hale abstained. Three out of four approved the meeting minutes.

3. Resolution
A. The Parking and Traffic Commission signed three resolutions to terminate the resident parking permit at
  the following locations:
 82nd Place from 8th Avenue to Park Circle; 74th Place from Victoria Avenue to West Boulevard; 75th
  Place from Victoria Avenue to West Boulevard; & West Boulevard from 74th Place to 75th Place; and 6th
  Avenue between Century Boulevard and Hardy Street
 The three resolutions are attached for reference.

4. Public Comments
A. A resident of Crenshaw Boulevard mentioned that non-residents come to park on the street when taking
  the Metro Line. Unfortunately, parking enforcement does not inspect daily, but on street sweeping days,
  the officers enforce the posted rules. The resident called for consistency and equality in the process of
  the Resident Parking Permit Program. Finally, The resident asked when the Resident Permit Parking
  Program sign would be installed on the residents' block.

B. An Oak Street resident asked the LAZ Parking Traffic Operations Manager if modifying the current citywide
  permit parking program has been discussed. No response was provided to the resident. The resident

  The City Traffic Engineer informed the resident that the street parking marking is not acceptable in the City
  as it eliminates parking spaces and the city cannot control people's behavior. The resident also raised
  concerns about the parking permit program in the City. Their concerns are the additional costs and the
  added stress to the community over the parking situation. Finally, the neighbor brought to the attention of
  the Parking and Traffic Commission that Eloy Morales, City Councilman District 3, has not communicated
  with the community after constant calls to withdraw the parking permit throughout the District.

C. The 6th Avenue resident drew the committee's attention to the broken curb and the city cones that were
  placed near the broken curb in December 2022. The resident wanted the City to repair the curb. Public
  Works staff informed the resident that the issue will be shared with the appropriate individuals.

D. The 82nd Place resident asked the panel what to do when there are no homes to ask for a signature to file
  a petition to end the Resident Parking Permit Program on the block. Mr. Thompson informed the resident
  that the street will not have signs nor will it be enforced.

5. Public Hearing
A. To amend the Residential Permit Parking Program on 95th Street between 8th Ave and 6th Ave
 The Parking and Traffic Commission approved the request to proceed with the voting process. The staff
  report was provided and read during the meeting. For reference, please visit the following link to get all
  the necessary information:
  https://www.cityofinglewood.org/AgendaCenter/ViewFile/Agenda/_01252023-3809
 The Department of Public Works will mail ballots to residents two weeks after the date of this meeting.
 The following comments were given as to why the resident does not support the parking program:
   There was no traffic impact during events.
   Residents and non-residents will not use the street to park and walk to the Sofi Stadium or anywhere.
   Residents rely heavily on street parking. The program is inconvenient and unreasonable.
   Thirteen (13) homeowners attended the meeting, and all do not support the program.
   The family owned more than two vehicles and disagrees with the decision to pay additional permits just
  for street parking.

DATE:  February 22, 2023

TO:  Parking and Traffic Commission

FROM:  Peter Puglese PE, TE, City Traffic Engineer

SUBJECT:  Public Hearing - Residential Permit Parking District 5D

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the Parking and Traffic Commission conduct a public hearing to do the
following:
1. Receive Public Comments regarding the elimination of Permit Parking District 5D; and
2. Provide direction to the City Engineer to not proceed with the elimination process of
  Residential Permit Parking District 5D.

BACKGROUND:
Prior to the formation of Residential Permit Parking District 5D (District), and since the opening
of SoFi Stadium (Stadium), residential parking has been extremely challenging in the District
because of its proximity to the Stadium.

In June 2020, the City Council adopted a Residential Permit Parking Program. The program
was enforced 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, with two-hour parking Monday through Sunday, 8
a.m. to 5 p.m. (Ordinance No. 20-09). The program was adopted to protect residential
communities more effectively and efficiently from non-resident vehicle intrusion.

On March 22, 2022, the Public Works Department received a petition requesting the elimination
of the District. Upon reviewing the petition, the Public Works Department confirmed that there
are 71 valid signatures (one signature per residential unit) out of the 1,159 households and
businesses within the District.

DISCUSSION:
Since the inception of the District, residents have had more parking opportunities in the District.
Fans from the Stadium are no longer parking in the nearby neighborhoods and taking valuable
on-street parking from the residents. In addition, once completed, the Intuit Dome (Clippers
Arena) will further burden the parking in the District (if eliminated). Permit Parking District 5D
protects residents from intrusive vehicle parking.

Residential Permit Parking Districts encourage residents to use their driveways, when available,
to park their vehicles so that those who do not have driveways can park on the street. Permit
Parking District 5D is one of the most densely populated areas in the City, and several
households have more than two (2) cars; therefore, Public Works Staff recommends that
Residential Permit Parking District 5D not be eliminated, and no further action should take place.

  NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING
  Petition for Elimination of Permit Parking in
  Residential Neighborhood
A petition has been submitted to the Inglewood Public Works Department requesting the termination of
Residential Permit Parking District 5D. Per Sections 3-75 to 3-79 of the Inglewood Municipal Code,
this matter will be presented to the Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission at the time and place
specified:

  Wednesday February 22nd, 2023 at 7:00 p.m.
  City Hall Lobby Community Room A
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

This notice is being mailed to all addresses fronting the subject street. Any interested person may
attend this meeting and speak on this matter.

  Purpose of Public Hearing
The purpose of this public hearing is to give all residents of the specific areas listed above an
opportunity to state their opinion of the subject matter.

The purpose of the Residential Permit Parking Program is to assure the availability to residents of some
on-street (curbside) parking spaces within a neighborhood where the patrons and/or employees of a
nearby commercial or industrial facility are otherwise using all available on-street parking spaces.

The Inglewood Parking and Traffic Commission will therefore be considering if the availability of on-
street parking is severely impacted in this manner and if the elimination of a Residential Permit Parking
District 5D would be warranted. If it is determined to be warranted, ballots will be mailed to each
household within the proposed parking district. A 75-percent (75 %) approval is required to eliminate
a Residential Permit Parking District.

If a Residential Permit Parking District is eliminated, all residents and visitors in this neighborhood will
not be restricted from parking on the public streets at any time; including during special events. If you
have any questions regarding this matter, or wish to express an opinion but are unable to attend the
public hearing, please contact the Inglewood Public Works Department at (310) 412-5333.

  Petición de Eliminación del Permiso de

Se ha presentado una petición al Departamento de Obras Públicas de Inglewood solicitando la
cancelación del Permiso de Estacionamiento Residencial dentro del Distrito 5D. De acuerdo con las
Secciones 3-75 a 3-79 del Código Municipal de Inglewood, este asunto se presentará a la Comisión
de Estacionamiento y Tráfico de Inglewood a la hora y lugar especificados:

  Miércoles 22 de Febrero de 2023 a las 7:00p.m.
  En la Sala Comunitaria A en el Primer Piso
  One Manchester Boulevard, Inglewood CA 90301

Este aviso se envía por correo a todas las direcciones que se encuentran al frente de la calle en
cuestión. Cualquier persona interesada puede asistir a esta reunión y hablar sobre este tema.

  Propósito de la Audiencia Pública
El propósito de esta audiencia pública es brindar a todos los residentes de las áreas específicas
enumeradas anteriormente la oportunidad de expresar su opinión sobre el tema. El propósito del
Programa de Permisos de Estacionamiento Residencial es garantizar la disponibilidad para los
residentes de algunos espacios de estacionamiento en la calle (bordillo) dentro de un vecindario donde
los clientes y/o empleados de una instalación comercial o industrial cercana utilizan todos los espacios
de estacionamiento disponibles en la calle.

Por lo tanto, la Comisión de Tráfico y Estacionamiento de Inglewood considerará si la disponibilidad
de estacionamiento en la calle se ve gravemente afectada de esta manera y si se justificaría la
eliminación de un Distrito 5D de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial. Si se determina que está
justificado, las boletas se enviarán por correo a cada hogar dentro del distrito de estacionamiento
propuesto. Se requiere una aprobación del 75 por ciento (75 %) para eliminar un distrito de
estacionamiento con permiso residencial.

Si se elimina un Distrito de Estacionamiento con Permiso Residencial, no se restringirá el
estacionamiento en las calles públicas a todos los residentes y visitantes de este vecindario en ningún
momento; incluso durante los eventos especiales. Si tiene alguna pregunta sobre este asunto o desea
expresar una opinión pero no puede asistir a la audiencia pública, comuníquese con el Departamento
de Obras Públicas de Inglewood al (310) 412-5333.
